text: Relationships are hard work, love requires constant effort. This is quite a popular statement, but honestly, I think this statement does more harm than good. Here's my take. Relationships should be either light and easygoing, or none at all. Because let's be real for a second. When people say relationships are hard work, what do they actually mean? They usually mean frequent arguments, repeated emotional talks, regular misunderstandings, slowly building frustration, and convincing yourself to stay even when you are unhappy. They mean stress, tension, and feeling like you are always fixing something that keeps breaking, and then this gets normalized. People start thinking that if a relationship feels heavy, draining, or exhausting, that's just how love is supposed to be. So they stay, they push harder, they try more, they go to therapy, read books, watch videos, and tell themselves it's worth it. How about this? Relationships should be either light and easygoing, or none at all. That doesn't mean zero effort, it means the effort is not a constant struggle. With the right person, things flow naturally. You don't need weekly crisis meetings, you don't need to negotiate basic respect, you don't feel anxious all the time wondering if you are doing something wrong. With the right partner, these agreements are occasional, not the foundation of the relationship. You feel stable, you feel respected, you actually enjoy being together instead of constantly working on being together. You see, life is hard, work is hard, building yourself as a person is hard. Your relationship shouldn't be another permanent source of stress on top of that. So when someone says relationships are hard work, I'd say this, choosing the wrong person makes relationships a hard work. Choosing the right one makes them light and easygoing.
